clue.text: Those midnight feasts schoolkids have in dormitories?

definitions.text: Those midnight feasts schoolkids have in dormitories?

parts.words: Those midnight feasts schoolkids have in dormitories?
parts.note: a midnight feast is a spread of food, and in a dormitory it is laid out on top of the beds

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look at illicit boarding-school feasts after lights out.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'spread' is a feast; one eaten on beds is a bed spread, which is also the cover laid over a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverlets thrown over beds are the literal items, punned on feasts spread out on mattresses.

clue.text: Trace our blunder to one Common Market official

indicators.note: blunder signals that trace our is made a mess of, coming out jumbled

explanation.surface: A mistake is traced to a Brussels bureaucrat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Common Market was the old name for the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat in the European administration is the official meant.

clue.text: So superior yet almost worthless

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective phrase for a coin of trifling value, the noun

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for upper class or superior

explanation.surface: Something top-quality yet of little value.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou was an old French coin of very small value.
explanation.definitionFit: An old French coin of tiny value, as in 'not a sou', stands for a trifling sum.

clue.text: Strong drink he imbibed cause of runny nose

indicators.note: the drink is said to have swallowed the word he, holding it inside

parts.note: rum is a strong spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man drinking spirits ends up with a streaming nose.
explanation.definitionFit: This watery mucus discharge is what makes a nose run.

clue.text: Newspaper piece needs rewriting to make it clear

indicators.note: rewriting suggests the words it clear are recast in a new order

explanation.surface: An editor says a report needs redrafting to be clearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' and 'to make' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A written item in a paper or magazine is a newspaper piece.

clue.text: Upholding police order weakens — it's irregular!

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
OM is the Order of Merit
to sap is to weaken

explanation.surface: Enforcing police orders only weakens them, a complaint about patchy policing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upholding' reverses all of CID + OM + SAPS, giving SPAS MO DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring in fits and starts rather than steadily is irregular.

clue.text: Run for water

explanation.surface: Two terse hints, one about running and one about water.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitive sprint is a contest of speed; a mill channel carrying a strong current of water is also called by this word.

clue.text: Priest converted hotels to underground refuges

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader, loosely a priest

indicators.note: converted says the hotels are turned into something new, the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric turns hotels into bunkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Burrows dug by small furry animals serve as their shelters below ground.

clue.text: Deadly illness doesn't end in ill-humour

indicators.note: the illness word is cut short, its final letter left off

parts.note: cholera is a deadly infectious disease

explanation.surface: A fatal disease that never finishes leaves people bad-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: In old medicine choler, yellow bile, was the humour causing anger; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritability or anger was attributed to excess yellow bile, one of the four humours.

clue.text: Genetic modification causing conflict with nature

indicators.note: the genetic modification is said to cause the word nature to come out jumbled

parts.note: GM is the standard abbreviation for genetically modified crops

explanation.surface: A warning that GM crops will put science at war with the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: GM plus NATURE make the eight letters; 'causing' asks for them to be shuffled into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated dispute or quarrel is a form of conflict between two sides.

clue.text: Having a pound. I take on the country

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a pound in their pocket sets out to conquer the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Albion is an old poetic name for Britain or England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic, poetic name for Britain, the land itself.

clue.text: Shield a lot of stars required

explanation.surface: A defence that apparently needs many stars to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required' is a link word joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman legionary's long oblong shield shares its Latin name with a small southern constellation.

clue.text: Special words used when sending out money to girl

indicators.note: sending out suggests the letters of money to girl are dispatched and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Particular vocabulary used when wiring cash to a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The specialised vocabulary of a field is its jargon.

clue.text: Thoroughly searched around, in seeking joint solution

indicators.note: the searched word goes round the little word in, which sits inside it

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Investigators who searched everywhere hope to reach a shared conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pooled together from several parties is a joint effort, made as one.

clue.text: The width of the lock

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair, so the width of a single strand is meant, not a canal lock or a door lock

explanation.surface: A measurement of a canal lock or a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a canal or a door; here it is a lock of hair, and the phrase means a tiny margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny margin, as narrow as one strand from the scalp, is the idiom being described.

clue.text: Innocent woolly lamb sees student off

indicators.note: woolly means muddled, so the words lamb sees come out jumbled
off adds that the student letter goes astray along with them

parts.note: L is the learner plate abbreviation for a student driver

explanation.surface: A fluffy lamb watches a student leave, without fault.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMB SEES plus L (student) are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free from fault or guilt is the state of being innocent.

clue.text: Step made, organising this collective flight

indicators.note: organising means the letters of step made are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Feet taking orderly steps as a crowd flees together.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'Steps' has one S too many for eight letters; 'Step made' rearranged gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mass rush of panicked animals or people is a flight by a herd.

clue.text: Weird rite a lunatic goes into — being tongue-tied

indicators.note: weird says the words rite a lunatic come out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone joins an odd ritual led by a madman and is left speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird' rearranges RITE A LUNATIC; 'goes into' and 'being' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to express oneself clearly in speech is a form of being lost for words.

clue.text: Very big? Dismantled, can be put into attic

annotationWithheld.why: Very big? Dismantled, can be put into attic (7): ATTIC holds the right letters bar I and N, but no clue word supplies IN (can = TIN gives eight letters); a word seems lost or misread and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Very big? Dismantled, can be put into attic

clue.text: Hard lump in stomach of animal that's eaten another animal

indicators.note: the first animal has swallowed the second, holding it inside

parts.note: a bear is a large mammal
a zo is a Himalayan cross of yak and cow, also spelt dzo

explanation.surface: Something hard found in a predator's belly after it ate its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: ZO, a yak hybrid, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of undigested matter found in an animal's gut was once prized as an antidote.

clue.text: Objective scented, rode unusually fast

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of rode appear in an unexpected arrangement

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A perfumed rider galloping off at an unusual pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' turns RODE into REDO; 'fast' is the noun, the forty-day Lent, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smelling strongly of a fragrance is perfumed with it.

clue.text: Re-open the account, in brief

explanation.surface: Bank instructions to reopen an account, briefly put.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb means start again; the noun, accented in French, is a summary or a CV.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart after a pause is to begin again; a short summary of a career or story is a précis of it.

clue.text: Contraption rotating on top of roof, at the outset

indicators.note: at the outset points to the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A whirling device mounted on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part of a machine is a mechanical device.

clue.text: Blue animal crossing the river

indicators.note: the animal stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a moose is a large deer
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An elk wading through a river, coloured blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour but means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or gloomy is being sullen and downcast.

clue.text: Public officials who've recorded impressions about polluted air

indicators.note: the notes go round the jumbled air, holding it inside

parts.note: notes are written records of what one observed

indicators.note: polluted means the word air is spoiled into a different order

explanation.surface: Officials who wrote up their observations on dirty air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorded impressions' means written notes, not marks pressed into a surface; 'who've' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lawyers authorised to witness and certify documents, officials serving the public.

clue.text: An impression left by traffic

parts.note: the impression is a groove worn into a road surface by wheels passing over and over

explanation.surface: A lasting effect that busy traffic has on people.
explanation.definitionFit: A track or furrow worn in the ground by repeated passage of wheels is that impression.

clue.text: Vehicle that was some distance back

indicators.note: back says the distance word is read from end to start

parts.note: a yard is a short distance of three feet

explanation.surface: A vehicle that was once some way behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses YARD; 'that was' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A low flat cart for heavy loads, as used by brewers, is a horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Pledges given about cruise site

indicators.note: about here means the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Deposits paid for holiday cruise destinations.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'sites' has one S too many; 'cruise site' rearranged gives the ten letters. 'given' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks or bonds are pledged as collateral, so financial guarantees are pledges.
